title: incremental-embeddings-storage-tiering-prd-2026-04-20
author: Aisha Gupta
content:
Overview

This Product Requirements Document (PRD) describes the requirements, design constraints, and rollout plan for Incremental Embeddings Storage Tiering (IEST). The feature enables tiered storage for customer embeddings with incremental compaction/migration, aiming to reduce long-term storage costs while preserving latency for high-value workloads.

Background and problem statement

Redwood Optimize and the embeddings APIs currently store customer embedding records in a single retention tier. As embedding usage grows, peak-cost exposure occurs for customers with large cold embedding stores (e.g., historic chat logs, archives) that are rarely queried but expensive to keep on fast SSD-backed volumes. Teams need a predictable, low-cost option that does not degrade query performance for recently active items.

Goals (success criteria)

- Reduce median storage cost per 1M embeddings for archival customers by 40% within 90 days of rollout.
- Maintain 95th percentile embedding lookup latency < 50ms for items in the hot tier.
- Support transparent migration between tiers without requiring customer SDK changes for read-only embedding retrievals.
- Provide observability: per-tenant storage breakdown, migration logs, and cost-savings estimates in Console.

Non-goals

- This PRD does not change vector index formats or alter approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms.
- It does not introduce new cross-tenant replication models.

Scope and user stories

Primary persona: platform engineers and data platform leads at customers who run large-scale semantic search and retrieval over historical data.

User stories:
1) As a customer platform engineer, I want embeddings older than 90 days to be automatically moved to a cold tier so my monthly bill decreases without manual intervention.
2) As an SRE, I want to observe migration throughput, error rates, and per-tenant cold item counts to troubleshoot performance regressions.
3) As a product analyst, I want a conservative cost-savings estimate per tenant exposed in Console before enabling tiering.

Requirements

Functional requirements:
- FR-1: Tier definitions. System must support at least three configurable tiers: hot (SSD NVMe), warm (standard SSD), cold (object storage with optional retrieval latency up to 2s).
- FR-2: Policy engine. Allow per-tenant TTL-based and access-frequency policies (e.g., move to cold after 90 days or after 30 days without a read).
- FR-3: Transparent reads. Reads for cold items must be transparently proxied: if a record is in cold, the service must fetch and return the embedding without requiring client-side changes.
- FR-4: Incremental migration. Support incremental background migration with rate limiting and backpressure to avoid saturating network or CPU on storage nodes.
- FR-5: Compaction and dedup. Provide a periodic compaction job to detect identical embeddings and collapse duplicates to save space in cold tier (subject to privacy labels).
- FR-6: Auditability. All tier transitions must be logged with timestamps, initiating policy, size delta, and owning tenant id.
- FR-7: Billing signals. Emit accurate per-tenant storage metrics to billing pipeline (GB-month per-tier) for downstream invoicing and usage UI.

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR-1: Latency. Reads served from hot tier: p95 < 50ms. Reads requiring cold retrieval should have p95 < 2s and p99 < 5s (target).
- NFR-2: Availability. Tiering control plane must be highly available: 99.95% monthly uptime.
- NFR-3: Cost. Cold tier should reduce per-GB monthly cost by >= 70% compared to hot tier.
- NFR-4: Security. All cold tier storage must respect tenant encryption settings (KMS/HSM) and maintain access controls identical to hot tier policies.

Design considerations and constraints

- Consistency: We will adopt eventual consistency for tier transition metadata; reads will consult a location index which is updated transactionally with migration initiations.
- Indexing: Vector indexes will maintain pointers to physical storage location; index updates during migration must be atomic to avoid stale pointer reads.
- Cross-region: For customers with multi-region deployment, migration must occur within the tenant region unless configured otherwise.
- Cost modeling: Provide simulators in Console to predict savings based on per-tenant read patterns and retention.

Architecture (high-level)

Components:
- Tiering Controller (service): Manages policies, schedules migrations, and exposes admin API.
- Location Index: Small metadata store (DynamoDB-style) mapping embedding_id -> tier & path. Strongly consistent updates for pointer swaps.
- Migration Worker Fleet: Horizontal workers that copy embeddings between tiers, verify checksums, and update Location Index.
- Tiered Storage Backends: Hot (SSD), Warm (networked SSD pool), Cold (object storage like S3-compatible with lifecycle classes).
- Read Proxy: Inference-serving layer enhancement to resolve location index and fetch from cold if required, with caching of recently accessed cold items into hot/warm cache.

Data model and example table

- embedding_record:
  - embedding_id (string)
  - tenant_id (string)
  - created_at (timestamp)
  - last_accessed_at (timestamp)
  - tier (enum: hot,warm,cold)
  - storage_path (string)
  - size_bytes (integer)

Migration policy configuration table (example)

| Policy name | Move after | Access threshold | Max daily throughput | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| default-archival | 90 days | 0 reads/30d | 50 GB/day | Conservative default for enterprise tenants |
| interactive-warm | 30 days | < 5 reads/7d | 200 GB/day | For datasets with occasional queries |
| cold-only | 365 days | 0 reads/365d | 10 GB/day | For long-term archival customers |

API changes and SDK compatibility

- Embeddings API: No breaking changes. New admin endpoints will be added to the Tenant Settings API to enable/disable tiering and to view estimates: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/tiering (enable/disable, policy).
- Read flow: SDKs and downstream apps continue to call embeddings.get(embedding_id). The server-side read proxy resolves location and fetches if necessary.
- Console: New pages under Storage > Embeddings for per-tenant breakdown, simulation tool, and manual migration control.

Migration and rollout plan

1) Internal prototype (Q2 2026)
   - Implement Location Index and worker prototype in staging; run on synthetic datasets; verify consistency model.
2) Beta (Q3 2026)
   - Invite 5 customers (mix of enterprise/startup). Enable warm tier only; monitor performance and cost. Provide opt-in UI and a migration dashboard.
3) Opt-in GA (Q4 2026)
   - Expand to general availability as opt-in. Add cost estimator in Console and alerts for failed migrations.
4) Auto-optimize (Q2 2027)
   - Turn on conservative auto-tiering default for new customers with explainer and opt-out.

Rollout safety controls and observability

- Rate limiting: Per-tenant migration throughput limits with global caps to protect backend.
- Abort patch: Ability to stop migrations globally within 30s of toggle.
- Telemetry: Metrics emitted: migration_bytes_total, migration_errors, tier_transition_count, per_tenant_cost_estimate, cold_read_latency_distribution. Logs: per-migration job trace with id and checksum.

Security, compliance, and privacy

- Encryption: All cold storage must support tenant KMS keys. For customers demanding on-prem cold storage, we will provide a private deployment option.
- Data minimization: Compaction must honor data retention policies and PII scrubbing rules; duplicates across tenants must never be merged.

Billing and pricing implications

- Billing: Introduce per-tier storage metrics exported to billing pipeline. Cold-tier storage will be metered as lower-cost GB-month. Migration traffic costs (egress) are included in data transfer billing for enterprise plans; for self-serve, migration transfer will be credited up to a threshold during migration windows.
- Pricing packaging: Consider a new add-on: Embeddings Archival Tier (discounted storage + migration credits). Outline for GTM will be created by Go-to-market.

Operational runbook (high-level)

- If migration error rate > 1% for 10 minutes: throttle migration workers to 10% and page oncall SRE.
- If cold read latency p95 > 3s: temporarily pin recent hot reads to warm cache, escalate to Storage team, and open a mitigation ticket.
- If location index inconsistency detected (pointer mismatch): fail-open to hot tier reads and schedule reconciliation job.

Open questions and decisions required

- Q1: What is the canonical compaction dedup policy across tenants that still meets privacy constraints? Decision owner: Data Platform.
- Q2: Should migration traffic be fully billable for self-serve customers? Decision owner: Finance and Product.
- Q3: Does the dedup compaction process require explicit tenant consent for certain regulated industries? Decision owner: Security & Compliance.

Dependencies

- Storage team: object storage lifecycle configuration and cold-storage pricing.
- Billing: implement per-tier metering and billing exports.
- Console: UI for policy configuration and simulator.
- SRE: migration worker fleet capacity and runbooks.

Owner and next steps

- PRD owner: Aisha Gupta (Product Manager)
- Engineering lead (tentative): Marco Alvarez
- Data platform liaison: Chen Li

Next steps:
1. Review and approve architecture decision points with Data Platform and Security (2 weeks).
2. Kickoff spike for Location Index and a minimal migration worker (4 weeks).
3. Prepare beta customer list and Console prototype (6 weeks).

Appendix: CLI examples and simulated cost calculation

- Simulated cost estimator (example):
  - Inputs: tenant_id, avg_embedding_size_bytes, historic_read_rate_per_day, retention_days
  - Output: projected_monthly_cost_by_tier

  Example payload:
  {
    "tenant_id": "acme-123",
    "avg_embedding_size_bytes": 1024,
    "historic_read_rate_per_day": 150,
    "retention_days": 365
  }

- Console will run the estimator and show a 3-line explainer with recommended policy.

End of document.
